newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM may visit Peru next week - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM may visit Peru next week - report.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto may visit Lima next week to thank Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori for resolving the hostage crisis, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
The Japanese and Peruvian governments have started talks on arranging Hashimoto's trip for May 9 to May 11, Jiji said.
For security reasons, the two governments were "secretly" making the arrangements, the news agency added.
But the trip could be postponed by one week, depending on the negotiations between the governments, Jiji said.
Japanese Foreign Ministry officials would not confirm the report.
Hashimoto said earlier this week that he wanted to visit Peru and express Japan's gratitude directly to Fujimori.

In a spectacular rescue operation, Peruvian troops stormed the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima on April 22, killing all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels. All but one of the 72 hostages held for 126 days, including all 24 Japanese diplomats and businessmen, were freed alive.
The Marxist rebels took over the residence on December 17 during a lavish reception held to celebrate the birthday of Japanese Emperor Akihito.
